recognize_zh: 周邊血液中散在數顆紅血球內含藍色粗大、分布不均的點狀顆粒（粗嗜鹼性點彩，coarse basophilic stippling），其中一顆略呈淡紫灰色，其餘紅血球大致正常，配合病史符合鉛中毒。
features: Scattered red cells containing coarse, irregular dark-blue punctate granules (coarse basophilic stippling)
Stippled cells are often slightly bluish-gray (polychromatic tinge) and some are ovoid
Granules distributed throughout the cell rather than clustered at one edge
Remaining red cells largely normocytic with central pallor; a few crenated cells and overlapping cells
No white cells in the field; occasional platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a population of predominantly normocytic red cells with central pallor, among which several red cells contain coarse, dark-blue punctate inclusions distributed throughout the cytoplasm, consistent with coarse basophilic stippling. Several stippled cells have a faint bluish-gray tint. A few crenated red cells are present, likely artifactual. No leukocytes are included in this field. Findings are consistent with coarse basophilic stippling; in the appropriate clinical context this supports lead poisoning, and blood lead and zinc protoporphyrin levels are recommended.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are fewer, larger angular granules clustered at the cell periphery and stain with Prussian blue, whereas stippling is numerous fine-to-coarse dots scattered throughout and iron negative.
These also produce coarse stippling, but thalassemia shows microcytosis and target cells and P5'N deficiency has hemolysis, so blood lead level, hemoglobin studies and enzyme assay separate them.
Superimposed platelets are single larger purple granular bodies with a halo and lie in a different focal plane, rather than multiple dots inside the cell.

ddx.dx: Malaria (early ring forms) or stain precipitate
ddx.vs: Ring forms have a chromatin dot with a cytoplasmic ring, and precipitate lies on top of cells and in the background, unlike intracellular evenly scattered stippling.
